channelTitle: Three nights before the assassination, Lincoln described his own funeral - Part 1
hook: This is not folklore - it comes from Lincoln's own bodyguard. Days before Ford's Theatre, the President described a dream he could not shake.
storyParts: April 1865 - the war was finally ending and Washington was celebrating. But inside the White House, Abraham Lincoln had been sleeping badly, haunted by a dream he later told to his bodyguard Ward Hill Lamon.
In the dream, Lincoln wandered the White House at night, hearing muffled sobbing but finding every room empty. Room after room, the weeping grew louder - and still no one was there.
At last he reached the East Room - and there lay a body on a catafalque, soldiers standing guard, mourners weeping around a coffin.
In the dream, Lincoln asked a soldier who had died. The soldier answered: the President - he was killed by an assassin. Lincoln woke shaken and told no one for days.
Three days later, on April 14, Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre. His body did indeed lie in state in the East Room - exactly as the dream had shown him.
cta: Do you think dreams can warn us, or was this just a terrible coincidence? Tell Grandma June below.
moral: Whether you call it warning or coincidence, it is the eeriest documented dream in American history.
seriesTitle: Lincoln's Last Dream - Grandma June Story Time
